The ambience is simple yet pleasant, suitable for families, office staff, and individuals alike. In a location where options for a proper sit down meal are rare, 3 Hrs Lunch stands out as a dependable spot for both lunch and dinner.

Overall, if you are near Antop Hill Post Monorail Station and looking for good food, reasonable prices, clean surroundings, and reliable service, 3 Hrs Lunch is definitely worth visiting.

However, the jalapeno rolls were disappointing. They were overly crispy and didn’t have any noticeable jalapeno flavor, making them not worth it. Dessert was a highlight, though – the warm Gulab Jamun was just perfect!

Service could definitely use some improvement. Although the restaurant wasn’t crowded as it was an off-peak time, it took quite a while for dishes to arrive. The jalapeno rolls came 20 minutes after ordering, almost at the end of my main course, and the Jeera Rice took another 10-15 minutes to be served.

Overall, it was an okay experience. Some dishes were delightful, but the slow service and a few underwhelming items left room for improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Neel
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Zen Bowl for lunch to try their food, as I had heard they serve both South Indian and Chinese dishes. My visit was good overall, though not everything was perfect.

When I reached the restaurant, the staff greeted me in a polite way. The place looked clean and comfortable. The menu has many choices, so it is nice if you are going with friends or family who like different types of food.

To start my meal, I ordered a dosa and medu vada. The dosa was crispy and light brown, with a potato filling inside. It was fresh and not very oily. The medu vada was soft and warm, but a little heavy. They served both items with coconut chutney and sambar. The chutney tasted fresh and the sambar was mild. I liked these dishes, but they were not as tasty as what you get in a pure South Indian restaurant. Still, it was good enough for a mixed menu place.

After that, I tried their Chinese food. I ordered vegetable fried rice, Manchurian gravy, and chicken fried rice. The vegetable fried rice had good flavor and plenty of fresh vegetables. It was not too oily, which I liked. The Manchurian was my favorite dish. The sauce was tasty, with a little sweetness and spice, and the vegetable balls were crispy on the outside. The chicken fried rice was also nice, with soft rice and pieces of chicken. The chicken could have had a little more flavor, but it was still enjoyable.

One thing I liked about Zen Bowl is that they have food for both vegetarians and non-vegetarians. This makes it easy if you are eating with people who have different food choices. The portions were big enough, and the prices were fair. You get good value for your money here.

featured_reviews.name: Sarbjeet Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mini Punjab, Antop Hill – A Mix of Comfort, Charm & Punjabi Flavours

Located in GTB Nagar, Sector V, Antop Hill, Mumbai, Mini Punjab stands out with its vibrant facade and warm interiors that reflect the spirit of Punjabi hospitality. The ambiance is welcoming – well-lit, clean, and cozy, with vibrant decor and neatly spaced-out seating that’s perfect for families or casual get-togethers.

Food Experience:
We ordered the Chicken Tikka, which looked tempting but sadly turned out to be a bit too dry for our liking – not as juicy or tender as expected. However, the Murgh Masallam more than made up for it. It was rich, flavorful, and paired beautifully with Jeera Rice, making it the highlight of our meal. The portion sizes are generous and filling. The mocktails and lassi menu also offer great variety – next time we’re keen to try their Dry Fruit Lassi or Guava Punch.

Service & Pricing:
Service is decent and quick enough even during rush hours. The staff is polite and attentive. As for pricing – it's affordable, especially considering the portions. Most mains range from ₹260–₹700 depending on quantity and meat choice. Breads like Laccha Paratha and Butter Cheese Garlic Naan are reasonably priced and fresh off the tandoor.

Verdict:
If you're looking for classic Punjabi dishes at pocket-friendly prices, this place is worth a visit. While not every dish hit the mark, the overall experience was satisfying. Ideal for families and groups who enjoy hearty North Indian meals in a clean, relaxed setting with the bonus of a TV screen to enhance the vibe.

Pro Tips:

Try their Murgh Masallam with Jeera rice or naan – definitely a winner.

The space is clean and Instagram-worthy, perfect for casual dining shots.

Parking may be a challenge during peak hours, plan accordingly.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic North Indian flavors with a homely touch, Oye Kaka is a place you shouldn’t miss. The vibe is simple yet inviting, making it perfect for a relaxed meal with friends or family.
The highlight here is definitely the rich and flavorful gravies — their butter chicken and dal makhani stand out with just the right balance of spices and creaminess. The kebabs are well-cooked and juicy, adding a great start to the meal. Pair it all with soft, freshly made rotis or naan, and you’re sorted.
Portion sizes are generous, and the pricing feels reasonable for the quality served. Service is quick and friendly, though it can get a bit busy during peak hours.
Overall, Oye Kaka delivers comfort food that hits the spot — a solid choice when you’re in the mood for hearty Punjabi cuisine. Do order their Kulchas and karare bhendi as per pics..follow for for more reviews.
